noAccess.title: No access to workspaces
noAccess.text: Workspaces, GPU time and JupyterHub come with projects. For most people a personal project from a budget that is approved at once is enough.

servers.title: Running servers
servers.intro: All own servers in JupyterHub, including those started there directly. Idle servers end by themselves: without GPU after 2 hours, with GPU after 30 minutes.
servers.name: Server
servers.stopMessage: “{{name}}” is stopped. Files in the home stay, unsaved changes in open notebooks are lost.

usage.title: Usage
usage.hint: What workspaces reserved from {{from}} to {{to}}: server hours, vCPU, RAM and GPU hours, home size. Collected every minute; today is not complete yet.
usage.csvHint: The grouping shown as CSV, with the measured values.
usage.explain: What is charged is the reservation (requested cores and memory), as with flavors in OpenStack. “CPU used” relates the measured use to it. Home GB-days: space used, measured hourly, the day's largest value counts; a project's storage is listed as “Projektspeicher”.

image.buildOnSave: The build starts on saving (usually 5–15 minutes).
image.label: Environment
image.hint: What is installed on the project’s servers, the same for every server type. The server type only chooses the hardware (CPU, CPU with GPU kernel, GPU).
image.finishedHint: A publicly pullable image. Built on one of our bases (FROM registry.gpu.services.dhbw.cloud/platform/base-…) it runs with everything; any other runs as it is (it needs jupyterhub-singleuser), without “CPU + GPU kernel”.
image.notDerived: This image is not built on one of our bases: it runs as it is, without “CPU + GPU kernel” and without the DHBW extensions.
image.gitHint: Built like Binder from requirements.txt, environment.yml, apt.txt and postBuild (top level, binder/ or .binder/) on the chosen base. The repository is in ~/projekte on start. A new version of the base triggers a rebuild; until a build is ready, the previous image stays.

projects.limits: Limits per person (at the same time)
projects.limitsHint: Counted is what one person runs in this project at the same time. 0 means no limit – except for GPUs, where 0 means no GPU.
projects.budgetsHint: Tighter limits within the project quotas, e.g. at most 40 vCPU hours per person in 7 days, so nobody uses up the quota alone. Windows in calendar days: “today”, 7 or 30 days including today, “total” since the project was created. Once a limit is reached, no server starts and running servers end within 5 minutes (the home stays).
projects.profilesHint: What members can choose when starting a server in JupyterHub. The platform sets the list; GPU types count against the project's GPU quotas.

storage.title: Storage (admins)
storage.hint: Workspace storage on JuiceFS: one volume per project with storage, plus homes from before the projects. Measured hourly.
storage.ofNode: of the node's {{total}} GB RAM · peak {{peak}} GB
storage.noReport: No measurement since the AI service last restarted; the next comes on the hour.
storage.explain: A project's limit is its workspace storage from the budget tree; a full volume refuses further writes. The metadata grow with the number of files (roughly 1 GB RAM per 2–3 million files); when RAM runs short, JuiceFS stops.

gpuHours.title: GPU use per hour
gpuHours.hint: How full the GPUs were, per hour in local time: colour = share held by workspaces; red outline = someone waited. Sampled every minute, kept 365 days.
gpuHours.hintProject: Who in the project held or waited for a GPU, and when, in the chosen period.
gpuHours.cell: {{day}}, {{hour}}:00–{{hour}}:59: workspaces {{share}}, gap filler {{inference}}, waiting on average {{avg}}, at most {{max}}
gpuHours.empty: No GPU use in this period.
gpuHours.explain: Counted is how long a GPU was assigned, not how much it computed. The gap filler (vLLM) uses a GPU as long as no workspace needs it and gives way at once. Waiting time: time in Kueue's queue until a GPU was free.

fleet.title: GPUs
fleet.intro: Every GPU node belongs to a pool (who the GPUs are for) and a tier (how large they are). Pool and tier make a GPU class: the budget tree grants it, and a server's start chooses it. More GPUs of an existing class need nothing in the tree; a node without pool takes no workspaces.
fleet.classesHint: Each class has its own queue and two resources in the budget tree. A class without nodes stays; its starts wait.
fleet.nodesHint: New GPU nodes appear here as soon as they are in the cluster. Changes apply to new pods within a minute; running ones stay where they are. The gap filler is an LLM that uses the GPU while no workspace needs it.
fleet.noNodes: No GPU nodes in the cluster.
fleet.poolsHint: “allgemein” is for everybody; a pool of its own is for GPUs only certain budgets should get (grant them in the tree only there). The id becomes part of the tree resources and is fixed then. A pool that lends gives idle GPUs to the other pools of the same tier and takes them back as soon as it needs them.
fleet.poolKeptClassesTip: A GPU class comes into being as soon as a node is assigned to the pool. It is a resource of the budget tree and projects may hold budget for it; that is why classes and their pool stay, even without nodes.
